exercise.name: Iso-Lateral Chest Press
library_steps: Load equal plates on each side and set the seat to chest height.
Press both handles forward until your arms are straight.
Let them come back slowly until you feel a chest stretch.
exercise.one_line_summary: Seated upright against the back pad, both hands on neutral (palms-in) handles. Picture 1: handles beside the chest, elbows out and a little behind the body; picture 2: arms pressed straight forward at shoulder height.

setup.target: Seat set so the handles sit at mid-chest; back flat on the pad, feet flat on the floor.

movement.start: 45 deg out, 20 deg behind the torso

muscles.emg: Seated chest press: pectoralis is the prime mover (S1).
Elbow extension through the press (S1, S3).
Anterior deltoid ~24 % MVIC with a neutral grip (S1).

muscles.role: Keep the trunk still against the back pad.

mistakes.mistake: Shoulders roll forward off the pad
mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Upper back leaves the pad at lockout.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Keeps the load on the chest and shoulders steady (S1 set-up).

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Hands at neck height at the start.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Seat height sets the line of push (S1).

sources.citation: Muyor JM, Rodriguez-Ridao D, Oliva-Lozano JM. Effect of grip width and grip orientation on muscle activity during the seated chest press. J Hum Kinet. 2023;87:23-34.
sources.what_it_gave: Seated machine chest press EMG: clavicular pectoralis ~30 % MVIC with a neutral grip, anterior deltoid ~24 %; grip orientation changes the split between the pec heads.

sources.citation: Rodriguez-Ridao D, Antequera-Vique JA, Martin-Fuentes I, Muyor JM. Effect of five bench inclinations on the electromyographic activity of the pectoralis major, anterior deltoid, and triceps brachii during the bench press exercise. Int J Environ Res Public Health. 2020;17(19):7339.
sources.what_it_gave: Bench inclinations 0-60 deg: 30 deg gives the highest clavicular pectoralis activity; anterior deltoid rises with incline.

sources.citation: Solstad TE, Andersen V, Shaw M, et al. A comparison of muscle activation between barbell bench press and dumbbell flyes in resistance-trained males. J Sports Sci Med. 2020;19(4):645-651.
sources.what_it_gave: Bench press activated pectoralis, anterior deltoid and triceps 8-81 % more than the dumbbell fly; in the fly the pec works with a fixed elbow.

clip_check.target: 45 deg out, 20 deg behind the torso -> 82 deg, straight forward (start 35-55, end 75-90)
100 deg (hands beside the chest) -> 8 deg (nearly straight, not locked) (start 85-110, end 0-15)

clip_check.check: Machine parts meet the hands/feet; levers keep their length
clip_check.target: moving rod lengths equal at start and end (+-1 cm)
